source.title: Is the rostro-caudal axis of the frontal lobe hierarchical?

confidence_rationale: Field-defining review with neuroimaging + anatomical + electrophysiological + developmental convergence for a rostro-caudal abstraction gradient (rostral=abstract/superordinate, caudal=concrete/proximate), including the asymmetric top-down control signature (anterior predicts caudal activation, not vice versa). Supports a granularity-matched goal hierarchy. Capped at 0.62 because 'abstraction' conflates several axes and the 2018 follow-up (Badre & Nee) argues the organization is discrete (3 zones) rather than a continuous unidimensional gradient -- a material qualification for any continuous-granularity model.
failure_signatures: The 2018 synthesis (Badre & Nee, TICS) revises the picture: evidence 'consistently supports three major functional subdivisions' that are 'functionally discontinuous, violating a linear, progressive rostro-caudal gradient' -- a continuous granularity axis is a modeling simplification, not the current consensus.

'Abstraction has been defined somewhat differently across these experiments' (domain-generality, relational integration, temporal abstraction, policy abstraction are conflated), so the mapping of a single goal-granularity axis onto the anatomical axis is not clean.
The review itself cautions that the gradient features 'do not, by themselves, require that the organization be hierarchical.'

mapping.source_claim_statement: Progressively more anterior/rostral lateral-PFC regions support control over progressively more abstract action representations (PMd/BA6 concrete -> BA44/45 -> mid-DLPFC/BA9/46 -> frontopolar/BA10 meta-level goals), with anterior regions exerting asymmetric top-down influence over caudal ones.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the candidate `granularity_matched_goal_hierarchy`: a superordinate goal and its concrete subgoals are represented at DIFFERENT granularity levels, and maintaining the abstract goal while executing concrete subgoals is supported by this cross-level organization. Extends ARC-051 (multi-level wanting hierarchy) with a representational-granularity axis -- the 'granularity systems' Daniel named. V4-scoped (REE has no explicit multi-scale goal-representation substrate yet).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rostro-caudal 'abstraction' is not identical to 'goal granularity' and may be discrete (~3 zones) rather than continuous. A REE model with a small number of discrete goal-granularity levels (superordinate / contextual-intermediate / concrete) maps better to current evidence than a continuous granularity scalar.
mapping.source_context: Human lateral prefrontal cortex; fMRI + anatomy + electrophysiology + development review.

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative review; mapping fidelity limited by the abstraction-conflation problem and the discrete-vs-continuous revision. Cite Badre & Nee 2018 alongside for honest scoping.
